note: The admin HTTP surface spine #2 adds. Not a JSON Schema and not under schemas/, for the reason recorded in spec/lifecycle-v1.json. T8 implements and tests this; T1 fixes the shape. dev/schema-fixture-check.py checks the invariants below that can be checked without an implementation — chiefly that nothing here is reachable by a cross-site form, and that cancellation agrees with spec/lifecycle-v1.json.

authorization.mechanism: Inherited, not re-declared. Every path sits under /admin, which UISecurityConfig already gates on userService.isAdmin. Spine #1 task 7 established this: a second matcher is a second place for an authorization rule to drift, and it was proven by moving the controller to /xadmin and watching a non-admin list, create and delete.
authorization.audience: Administrators only. Bundle bytes, build logs and source are NOT reachable by a content viewer: canAccess grants the right to run content, never to read what it was built from.
authorization.signed_out: Redirected to log in, as everywhere else under /admin. Never served.

csrf.rule: No endpoint may accept a media type an HTML form can produce. That is the whole defence, because ShinyProxy enables CSRF protection for POST /login alone, so a session-authenticated admin on a hostile page is otherwise submittable.
csrf.consequence: The bundle upload is a raw application/gzip body and explicitly NOT multipart/form-data, which is the obvious way to build an upload and the one a cross-site form can forge. A non-safelisted content type forces a CORS preflight, which is denied for an origin the deployment has not configured. Not 'never granted': ContainerProxy enables CORS when proxy.api-security.cors-allowed-origins is set (WebSecurityConfig.java:126-128), and those origins are mapped with credentials across /**. The guarantee is against unconfigured origins, and a deployment that lists an origin has chosen to trust it.
csrf.required_header_rationale: Belt to the content-type braces. A custom header cannot be set by a cross-site form at all, and setting one from fetch() forces a preflight. It costs one header and does not depend on message-converter configuration that nothing in this repository owns.

endpoints.notes: Creates the bundle row in UPLOADING and returns its id. Metadata travels as JSON here so the byte upload carries none, which keeps the binary endpoint a pure stream.

The bytes. Accepted only while the bundle is UPLOADING, which is the only state with no committed receipt. Streamed to object storage under the configured limits and never buffered whole; Content-Length is a claim, checked against the bytes actually read.
endpoints.replay: PUT is idempotent in the sense that matters -- it never creates a second bundle and never rewrites committed bytes -- and NOT in the sense of 'send it again and it works'. Once the receipt is committed the bytes are immutable and the bundle has left UPLOADING, so a repeat PUT is refused with 409 carrying the bundle's current state. A client whose response was lost recovers with GET bundle.status, not by uploading again: re-reading is the safe recovery and re-writing is not. Different bytes at the same id are the same 409 -- replacing content means a fresh bundle id, because a bundle id names particular bytes that a build may already have read. Concurrent PUTs to one id serialise; the loser gets 409. A PUT abandoned before its receipt leaves the bundle in UPLOADING and its partial object to the one-hour incomplete-upload rule, so a later PUT restarts it cleanly.

endpoints.notes: Bundle state and, when REJECTED, the named rule that rejected it.
202, never 200: it returns a build id and a status URL and does not wait for an image. Body names a VALIDATED bundle and an idempotency key; the key stops an HTTP retry becoming a second attempt.

Cursor-paginated over committed chunks. text/plain is the curl view and exists so an admin can read a failing build before any UI does. Log text is escaped and terminal control sequences are neutralised; it is never interpolated into HTML.
Resumable from a cursor, bounded subscriber queue, keepalive and a terminal event. A slow or vanished client must not stall the build.
POST, not DELETE: cancelling is not deleting, and nothing is removed. 202 because cancellation during execution completes only once the worker is confirmed stopped.

cancel_refused_rationale: 409 rather than a silent no-op. A push may already have produced a digest, so a cancel racing publication is how an image comes to exist with no row describing it. This list must agree with spec/lifecycle-v1.json: a state named here must have no transition to CANCELLED.

shapes.note: Added by T8 (a), signed off by the user on 2026-10-20 (WORKPLAN-BUNDLES T8 plan, ad2d195 + c50e4fa). Additive: every key above this one is T1's and unchanged. What T1 left open -- bodies, errors, the log cursor and formats, the stream, the cancel replies -- is fixed here, and dev/schema-fixture-check.py holds it consistent with the frozen keys and spec/lifecycle-v1.json. The Java side holds its enums and controllers to this file.

data.message: no detail beyond a correlation id

envelope.why: ContainerProxy's ApiResponse, as spine #1's /admin/content uses. data is an object so a client branches on code, never on message text. Spine #1's own string-valued errors are left as they are.
envelope.not_this_envelope: A non-admin's 403 and a signed-out caller's redirect to log in are upstream's responses, not this envelope.

shapes.strict_request_bodies: An unknown field in a JSON request body is 400 BAD_REQUEST, as in the manifest.

untyped_body.rule: A body with no Content-Type is sendable cross-site without a preflight (navigator.sendBeacon; fetch no-cors with an untyped Blob). consumes reads it as application/octet-stream and refuses it.

untrusted_text.json: Responses are written with every non-ASCII character escaped, so the bytes on the wire are ASCII: a bidi override or a C1 control arrives as \uXXXX, never raw.
untrusted_text.text: The text view replaces Cc (except tab), Cf, Zl, Zp and default-ignorable code points (publisher.names.InvisibleCharacters) with \x{HEX}.

UPLOAD_INCOMPLETE.why: fewer bytes than Content-Length arrived; the bundle stays UPLOADING and the same PUT may be sent again

BUNDLE_NOT_FOUND.why: also another content item's bundle: no oracle

BUNDLE_ARCHIVE_CONFLICT.why: a replay's bytes differ from the archive already stored; make a new bundle

RETRY_BUNDLE_MISMATCH.why: retryOf reuses its attempt's bundle; naming another is a different request

STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE.why: the store's outcome unknown, 400 IncompleteBody, or throttling past the SDK's retries; never a verdict on the bundle

request.bundleId: uuid; optional only when retryOf is given
request.retryOf: optional uuid of a terminal attempt of this content

log_states_added.none: the attempt ended without running (cancelled or superseded while QUEUED): it never has a log
log_states_added.expired: terminal past the 90-day log retention with no final record left
log_states_added.storage_unavailable: the log store could not be read; the status still answers, as the stream does (stream.storage_outage)

query.before: a buildId from a previous page's next

query.limit: records; ndjson default 1000, max 10000; text unlimited

cursor.form: <chunk sequence>.<record index>, both decimal, no leading zeros
cursor.matched: whole: java.util.regex matches(), never find(); $ alone matches before a final newline (dd46cac-F2)
cursor.opaque: Documented so a person can read one; a client never builds one.
cursor.served_up_to: what the log advertises: final.json once it exists, else index.json; never past a hole
cursor.ahead_of_index: not an error: replay returns nothing, the stream waits

line.cut: true, only when the line was shortened

log_records.stored_marker_renamed: HeadTailLog stores the marker as {"cut":{...}}; it is served as gap so the two meanings of cut do not share a key
log_records.text_line: <n right-aligned> | <text>, ' [cut]' appended to a shortened line
log_records.text_platform_lines: ----- skald: ... ----- (no ' | ', so build output cannot pass for one)

stream.event_ids: the record's cursor, on line and gap
stream.after_end: the server closes; a reconnect gets end again at once
stream.model: pull: each subscriber reads committed chunks from storage when its previous write has gone out. Nothing the build writes waits for a reader.
stream.supersedes: the build.logs.stream note's 'bounded subscriber queue': there is no queue at all, which is the stronger form of the same bound. The frozen note is left unedited.
stream.storage_outage: a state event with logState storage_unavailable, then retries with backoff until the connection limit

cancel_replies.why: superseded: cancelled with no request of its own

shapes.cancel_replay: A retry reports the cancel's current outcome; it never makes a second cancel or a different transition.

upload_commit_point.put: The row moves UPLOADING -> VALIDATING under its lock, with object_key, object_sha256 and object_bytes from the archive put or the stage (ii) read-back. receipt.json is NOT written by the PUT.
upload_commit_point.validation_is_claimed: A VALIDATING row is claimed work: FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, a generation-fenced lease (60 s, renewed every 20 s), re-run by any instance when the lease lapses; a full pool makes rows wait and never refuses a PUT (6a23bcb-F1).
upload_commit_point.lifecycle_correction: spec/lifecycle-v1.json says VALIDATING means 'bytes are complete and the receipt is committed'. Read it as: the bytes are complete and their digest is on the row; receipt.json is written last, by validation (BundleWriter.commit, BundleReceipt). The frozen text is left unedited (c50e4fa-F1).

upload_replay.action: written as a first PUT would
the body is hashed without storing; the stored archive is read back once and hashed; a match moves the row to VALIDATING with the read-back digest

validation_claims.not_counted: a claim released after a recorded storage error
validation_claims.precedence_why: a recorded storage error is the observed cause, so it wins; a short outage must never read as a poison bundle (95e2185-F1)

rejection_rules_added.UPLOAD_ABANDONED: UPLOADING past its upload deadline (lifecycle: upload abandoned past its deadline)
rejection_rules_added.VALIDATION_STORAGE: VALIDATING past its deadline with a storage failure recorded; names the store, not the bundle
rejection_rules_added.VALIDATION_STALLED: VALIDATING past its deadline with nothing finished and nothing recorded: no validator ran
rejection_rules_added.VALIDATION_INTERRUPTED: its validation's lease lapsed max-claims times (claimed, never released, expired: the validator died): something in the bundle ends validators
rejection_rules_added.S9: the manifest's type differs from content.type
